mcpServers.description:
MCP servers scoped to this preview, keyed by scope (`shared` / per-agent / etc.).
Use the camelCase key `mcpServers` (preferred) or the snake_case alias `mcp_servers`. Empty by default.

parent_harness_id.description:
Parent harness to extend. When set, its prompt, capabilities, and MCP servers are
merged with the fields in this request before rendering.

system_prompt.description:
System prompt to render as the base prompt for the preview. Optional:
omit to preview a harness that contributes no base prompt of its own.

PrincipalKind.description:
Class of principal that can hold permissions or own resources. `system`
is reserved for platform-internal callers and is never minted via the
public API.

PrincipalSummary.description:
Compact view of a principal — id + kind + the subject-id pointer back
into the user/virtual-user row. Used wherever a full `Principal`
would be redundant (e.g. as a sub-field of a session or audit record).

name.description: Human-readable name. Safe to render in user-facing messages.

ProjectorRunQuery.description:
Query parameters for a manual `POST /v1/reports/projector/run` invocation —
the cap on how many outbox rows one run is allowed to claim.

limit.description: Maximum number of items returned in this page.

ProjectorRunResult.description:
Outcome of one projector run — how many outbox rows it claimed,
completed, and failed. Returned by manual `POST /v1/reports/projector/run`
calls and useful for backfill scripting.

claimed.description: Number of outbox rows claimed by this run.

completed.description: Number of claimed rows that completed successfully.

failed.description: Number of claimed rows that failed and will be retried (or moved to `failed` after retry limit).

Provider.description:
LLM Provider entity (API keys never exposed)
This is the persisted provider entity, separate from the runtime provider trait.

api_key_set.description: Whether an API key is configured. The key itself is never returned.

base_url.description: Custom base URL for self-hosted / proxied providers. `None` means use the provider's default endpoint.

created_at.description: Timestamp when this provider was created (RFC 3339).

last_synced_at.description: Timestamp of the most recent successful model sync from the provider's API (RFC 3339).

managed.description:
Whether this provider is host-managed (EVE-810). A managed provider is
provisioned by the host/embedder; the OSS API rejects tenant PATCH/DELETE
on it (403). Read-only to org admins. Defaults to `false`.

models_reviewed_at.description:
When someone last reviewed this provider's discovered models (RFC 3339).
A discovered model created later that is still disabled is reported as
`is_new` on the model. `None` means never reviewed.

name.description: Human-readable provider name. Safe to render in user-facing messages.

provider_type.description: Provider implementation type (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, etc.).

oneOf.description:
Extra headers and diagnostics options applied to every request sent to
this provider. `None` when the org configured nothing.

status.description: Current lifecycle status of this provider.

oneOf.description:
Resolved trace/observability link configuration: the driver's default
templates overlaid with this provider's stored overrides. `None` when the
driver exposes no dashboard and the org configured nothing.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when this provider was last updated (RFC 3339).

ProviderOpaqueContent.description:
Provider-native assistant content retained for lossless replay.

Drivers use this only when a provider requires its response content to be
sent back without reconstruction. The portable text, reasoning, and tool
call fields remain the fallback for other providers.

provider.description: Provider that owns and can replay this content.

ProviderRequestHeader.description: One extra HTTP header sent with every request to a provider connection.

name.description: Header name, e.g. `x-gateway-tenant`.

ProviderRequestOptions.description:
Per-connection request options: what an org wants added to every outbound
request to this provider, beyond endpoint and credentials.

These are connection-level on purpose. A gateway header or a diagnostics
opt-in describes the *service* an org talks to, not one agent's behavior, so
it belongs next to the base URL and credentials rather than on every agent.

cache_diagnostics.description:
Ask the provider to explain unexpected prompt-cache misses. Honored by
drivers with a diagnostics protocol (today: Anthropic's
`cache-diagnosis` beta); ignored elsewhere.

headers.description:
Extra HTTP headers added to every request to this provider. They
override the driver's and the connection's own headers by name, but
connection-level headers (`host`, `content-length`, ...) are ignored.

ProviderResponse.description: Provider info for the connections UI

capabilities.description: Product features that can consume this connection.

description.description: Provider description.
description.example: Connect your repositories

display_name.description: Provider display name.

oneOf.description: Fields required for API key providers.

ProviderTraceConfig.description:
Configuration for linking from the chat UI to a provider's observability
dashboard ("trace"/"logs").

This is provider-agnostic: any driver with a dashboard can supply default
templates (see [`DriverId::default_trace_templates`]), and an org enables
links per provider once it has confirmed logging is on for that account.
URL templates support the `{response_id}`, `{session_id}`, `{turn_id}` and
`{model}` placeholders, so the same mechanism works for OpenRouter today and
for third-party observability backends (Langfuse, Helicone, ...) via an
override.

enabled.description:
Whether trace links should be shown for this provider. Defaults to
`false`: vendors typically do not retain trace content unless logging is
explicitly enabled, so the org opts in once that is set up.

generation_url_template.description:
URL template for a single generation's trace, e.g.
`"https://openrouter.ai/logs?id={response_id}"`.

session_url_template.description:
URL template for a session's grouped trace, e.g.
`"https://openrouter.ai/logs"`.

ProvidersConfigResponse.description:
Provider resource config: caller policies plus the credential schemas the UI
renders per driver.

drivers.description: Per-driver credential schemas, ordered by driver id.

policies.description: Map of policy ID → whether the caller satisfies it.

QuestionAnswersRequest.description: Request to answer a pending `ask_user` question set.

answers.description: One answer per asked question, keyed by question id.

status.description:
What the person did. `answered` carries answers; `declined` is a finished
decision the model must not re-ask.

tool_call_id.description:
The `ask_user` tool call being answered. Optional: when omitted the one
pending question set on the session is used.

QuestionAnswersResponse.description: Result of answering a pending question set.

answered_by.description: Who the server attributed the outcome to.

duration_ms.description: Duration of the reason phase in milliseconds

oneOf.description: Token usage from the LLM call

ReasonItemData.description:
Data for `reason.item` event.

Durable record of one provider reasoning artifact.

Carries identity and curated summary text only. Opaque replay state
(signatures, encrypted reasoning context) is deliberately absent: it is
state the driver hands back to the provider, not content, and it must not
reach an event stream or any API surface. Plaintext chain-of-thought is
likewise never persisted here.

item_id.description: Provider-assigned identifier for the reasoning item.

model.description: Model identifier reported by the provider, if known.

provider.description: Provider that produced the reasoning item (e.g., "openai").

summary.description:
Safe summary text segments curated by the provider. Never includes
plaintext reasoning content.

token_count.description: Per-item reasoning token count, when the provider reports one.

turn_id.description: Turn ID this reasoning item belongs to.

ReasonRecoveredData.description:
Data for the `reason.recovered` event (EVE-532).

Emitted by `ReasonAtom` when it detects an in-flight partial assistant
message from a previous worker execution and applies the ContinuePartial
recovery policy.

accumulated_len.description: Character length of the persisted accumulated text.

turn_id.description: Turn ID the partial belonged to.

oneOf.description: Agent ID being used (optional)
Metadata about the model being used

ReasonThinkingCompletedData.description:
Data for reason.thinking.completed event

Emitted when extended thinking completes and the model transitions
to producing the final response. Contains the complete thinking content.

turn_id.description: Turn ID this thinking belongs to

ReasonThinkingDeltaData.description:
Data for reason.thinking.delta event (extended thinking content from models like Claude)

This event streams incremental thinking/reasoning content from models that support
extended thinking mode (e.g., Claude with thinking enabled). The thinking content
represents the model's chain-of-thought reasoning before producing the final response.

accumulated.description: Accumulated thinking text so far (convenience for UI)

delta.description: The thinking delta (new thinking text since last delta)

turn_id.description: Turn ID this delta belongs to (for correlation)

ReasonThinkingStartedData.description:
Data for reason.thinking.started event

Emitted when extended thinking begins during reasoning phase.
This signals the model is using chain-of-thought reasoning.
UI can show a "thinking" indicator.

turn_id.description: Turn ID this thinking belongs to

oneOf.description:
Effort level for reasoning.

Typed rather than free-form: the effort taxonomy is closed, and each
driver previously re-parsed the string with its own case handling, which
let `minimal` silently mean "no reasoning" on budget-based models.

ReasoningContentPart.description:
One provider-issued reasoning artifact, ordered in `Message.content`
alongside text and tool calls.

Ordering is the point. Providers interleave reasoning with text and tool
calls, and every current provider requires its artifacts replayed in the
position it issued them: Anthropic verifies each thinking block against its
own `signature`, OpenAI keys reasoning items by the `item_id` it issued and
expects them adjacent to the item they precede, and Gemini binds a
`thoughtSignature` to a specific function call. A flattened per-message
field cannot express any of that, so this is a content part.

`signature` and `encrypted` are opaque provider artifacts. They are carried
verbatim and never interpreted, never rendered, and never published on an
API surface — see [`ReasoningContentPart::to_public`].

bound_tool_call_id.description:
Id of the tool call this artifact is bound to, when the provider scopes
it that way (Gemini attaches a thought signature to one function call).

provider.description:
Provider that produced this artifact (e.g. `anthropic`, `openai`).
Replay is only valid against the provider that issued it.

signature.description:
Provider signature over this specific block (Anthropic thinking
signature, Gemini `thoughtSignature`). Opaque.

oneOf.description: Readable reasoning, when the provider exposes any.

tokens.description: Reasoning tokens attributed to this artifact, when reported.

ReasoningEffort.description: Reasoning effort level for models that support it

ReasoningEffortConfig.description: Reasoning effort configuration for a model

default.description: Default reasoning effort for this model

values.description: Available reasoning effort values for this model

ReasoningEffortValue.description: Named reasoning effort value for UI display

name.description: Display name (e.g., "Low", "Medium")

ReasoningState.description: Persisted with assistant messages and native compaction checkpoints.

oneOf.description: Original request-level effort preserved throughout this epoch.
Effort currently active after ordered configuration updates.

epoch.description: A new epoch starts when switching model/provider or entering this mode.

oneOf.description:
Verbatim chain-of-thought exposed by the provider (Anthropic extended
thinking, Gemini thought parts, Chat Completions `reasoning_content`).

Provider-curated summary segments, not raw chain-of-thought (OpenAI
Responses `summary_text`). Safe to display; never the model's own words.

The provider withheld the content (Anthropic `redacted_thinking`). The
artifact must still be replayed verbatim, so the part keeps its
signature/encrypted payload while carrying no readable text.

ReasoningText.description:
Readable reasoning text, in the form the provider actually exposes.

Providers differ in *what* they are willing to show, and collapsing that
difference loses the one thing a consumer needs to know: whether it is
looking at the model's own words or a curated gloss of them.

RecoveryMode.description: Recovery mode chosen by the ContinuePartial classifier (EVE-532).

RedactionOptions.description: Redaction controls. Secret scrubbing is always applied regardless of these.

redact_content.description:
When true, replace message text/tool content with a placeholder, keeping
only structure (roles, tool names, ids). Secret scrubbing still runs.

ReportColumn.description:
One column header in a `ReportResult`. The ordered `columns` list
declares the key set of each row in `rows`.

kind.description:
Whether this column is a grouping `dimension` or an aggregate
`measure` — the same distinction made on `ReportQuery`.

name.description: Column name as it appears in `rows`.

ReportColumnKind.description: Whether a `ReportColumn` is a grouping dimension or an aggregate measure.

ReportExport.description:
Serialized export of a report's data, ready to stream to a caller as a
download. Carries the rendered payload plus the MIME/filename metadata
a client needs to save it.

as_of.description: Timestamp the underlying data was materialized (RFC 3339). Useful for "as of" footers.

content.description: Serialized payload as a UTF-8 string. Caller streams this to the client.

content_type.description: MIME type matching `format` (`text/csv` for CSV exports).

filename.description: Suggested filename for the download (includes the extension matching `format`).

freshness_lag_ms.description: How stale the data is relative to `now()`, in milliseconds. `None` when freshness can't be determined.

ReportExportFormat.description:
Output format for a report export. `Csv` emits a header row plus one
row per result; `Json` emits an envelope with the same shape as
`ReportResult`.

ReportFilter.description:
One predicate filter applied to the dataset before aggregation.
Combined with other filters via logical AND.

field.description: Field to filter on. Must be a filter field exposed by the dataset (see `filter_fields` in the catalog).

op.description:
Comparison operator. Determines the expected shape of `value`
(scalar for `eq`/`neq`/`gt`/`gte`/`lt`/`lte`, array for `in`).

value.description:
Comparison value. Type depends on `op`: a scalar for `eq`/`neq`/`gt`/`gte`/`lt`/`lte`,
an array for `in`. Example for `op = in`: `["completed", "failed"]`.

ReportFilterOp.description:
Comparison operator used in a `ReportFilter`. The `In` variant takes a
JSON array as its value; all others take a scalar.

ReportOrderBy.description:
One sort clause applied to the aggregated result. Either `dimension`
OR `measure` is set (mutually exclusive), never both.

dimension.description: Dimension name to sort by. Mutually exclusive with `measure`.

measure.description: Measure name to sort by. Mutually exclusive with `dimension`.

ReportQuery.description:
Semantic query a caller submits to the reporting layer. The backend
compiles this to its native query language, scopes it to the calling
org, and returns a `ReportResult`.

dataset.description: Dataset name to query (see `GET /v1/reports/catalog` for the list of available datasets).

dimensions.description: Columns to group by. Empty list returns one aggregate row.

limit.description: Maximum number of rows to return (defaults to 100).

measures.description: Aggregations to compute (count, sum, avg, etc.). Empty list returns row counts only.

order_by.description: Sort spec applied after aggregation. Empty list yields unspecified order.

time_range.description: Time window for the query. The dataset selects which timestamp column the range applies to.

ReportResult.description:
Materialized result of a report query — column metadata, rows, and the
freshness of the underlying data.

as_of.description:
Timestamp the underlying data was materialized (RFC 3339). Useful as
an "as of" footer when rendering — distinct from when the query ran.

columns.description:
Column metadata in the same order as the entries of each row in
`rows`. Use the `kind` field to tell dimensions from measures.

freshness_lag_ms.description:
How stale the data is relative to the server's wall clock at query
time, in milliseconds. `None` when freshness can't be determined
(e.g. backends that don't track projector lag).

rows.description:
Result rows. Each row is a JSON object keyed by column name; cell
types match the underlying dataset (numbers for measures, strings
or numbers for dimensions). Length is capped by `ReportQuery.limit`.

ReportTimeRange.description:
Half-open time window applied to the dataset's primary timestamp column
during a report query. `from` is inclusive, `to` is exclusive.

ReportingBackfillRequest.description:
Request body for the `reporting_backfill` operation — enqueues source
rows into the reporting outbox for the projector to re-materialize.

limit.description: Maximum number of outbox rows to enqueue across all source types. Defaults to 1000.

ReportingBackfillResult.description:
Result of a `reporting_backfill` call — per-source counts of outbox rows
enqueued for re-projection.

enqueued.description: Total number of outbox rows enqueued across all source types.

ReportingDiagnostics.description:
Point-in-time health snapshot of the reporting layer — projector
freshness plus outbox processing health. Returned from
`GET /v1/reports/admin/diagnostics`.

generated_at.description:
Server-side wall-clock timestamp when this snapshot was assembled
(RFC 3339). Use as the "as-of" for any displayed lag metrics.

outbox.description:
Reporting outbox health — counts of pending/processing/failed/
completed rows plus a sample of the most recent failures.

projector_lag.description:
Per-dataset projector freshness. One entry per active reporting
dataset; missing datasets mean the projector hasn't produced any
rows yet.

ReportingOutboxDiagnostics.description:
Aggregate health of the reporting outbox — the queue of source rows
waiting to be projected into fact tables.

completed.description: Outbox rows that have completed processing successfully.

failed.description: Outbox rows that have failed (exceeded retry limit).

failed_rows.description: Sample of the most recent failed rows for operator inspection.

oldest_pending_at.description: Timestamp of the oldest `pending` row (RFC 3339). `None` if no rows are pending.

pending.description: Outbox rows waiting to be claimed by a projector.

org_id.description: Public ID of the organization that owns the resource.

ResolvedSandboxSpec.description:
Session-pinned specification. Every security- and recovery-relevant default has
been made explicit.

target.description: Exact target pinned for the Session.

template_revision_id.description: Reusable revision from which this complete snapshot was copied.

ResourceConfigResponse.description:
Response type for per-resource config endpoints.

Every resource exposes `GET /v1/{resource}/config` returning this type.
UI uses it to gate controls (create/edit/delete buttons, admin panels).

policies.description: Map of policy ID → whether the caller satisfies it.

active_session_count.description: Sessions in a running state right now.

avg_session_duration_ms.description: Average session duration in milliseconds. `None` when `session_count` is 0.

execution_count.description: Total number of agent executions (turns) recorded across all sessions for this resource.

first_session_at.description: Timestamp of the first session for this resource (RFC 3339). `None` if no sessions exist.

idle_session_count.description: Sessions in an idle state right now (created but no recent activity).

last_execution_at.description: Timestamp of the most recent execution (turn) for this resource (RFC 3339). `None` if no executions exist.

last_session_at.description: Timestamp of the most recent session for this resource (RFC 3339). `None` if no sessions exist.

session_count.description: Total number of sessions ever created for this resource.

started_session_count.description: Sessions that have started at least one turn.

total_actual_cost_usd.description:
Cumulative provider-reported actual cost in USD across all sessions
(e.g. OpenRouter's `usage.cost`). Excludes generations with no reported cost.

total_cache_creation_tokens.description: Cumulative cache-write tokens across all sessions (charged when first writing a cache entry).

total_cache_read_tokens.description: Cumulative cache-read tokens across all sessions (where the provider supports prompt caching).

total_cost_usd.description:
Cumulative best-effort cost in USD across all sessions: actual provider
cost where reported, otherwise the price-table estimate. Actual takes priority.

total_estimated_cost_usd.description:
Cumulative price-table estimated cost in USD across all sessions.
Excludes generations with no profile cost data.

total_input_tokens.description: Cumulative LLM input tokens billed across all sessions.

total_output_tokens.description: Cumulative LLM output tokens billed across all sessions.

total_session_duration_ms.description: Cumulative session wall-clock duration in milliseconds across all sessions.

waiting_for_tool_results_session_count.description: Sessions currently paused waiting for client-side tool results.

kind.description: Entity kind, needed only for kinds whose ids have no prefix.

entity.description: The entity after the restore, as its update command returned it.

warnings.description: Secrets kept at their current value that differ from the revision.

ResumeSessionResponse.description: Result of resuming budgets paused for a session.

description.description: Omit to preserve; send null to clear.
description.example: Larger recoverable workspace for repository builds

display_name.description: Replacement display name; omit to preserve the current value.

spec.description: Complete specification stored as the next immutable revision.

RiskLevel.description:
Risk classification for capabilities (TM-AGENT-005).

Used to enforce approval requirements when assigning capabilities.

RotateAgentKeyRequest.description: Request to rotate an agent key.

overlap_hours.description: Hours the replaced secret keeps working (0 to 168, default 24).

RunBucket.description: Turns started and failed in one bucket.

RunSummary.description: Aggregate metrics for a completed eval run.

pass_rate.description: Fraction of cases that passed, 0.0 to 1.0.

total.description: Total number of cases in the run.

content.description: Message content as array of content parts (text, images, tool calls, tool results)

oneOf.description: Runtime controls (model, reasoning, etc.)

created_at.description: Timestamp when the message was created

oneOf.description: External actor identity (for messages from external channels like Slack)

metadata.description: Message-level metadata

oneOf.description:
Execution phase for this message.

Helps LLMs distinguish between intermediate working commentary and completed
answers in multi-step tool-calling flows. Only set on agent (assistant) messages.
Providers with native phase support (OpenAI GPT-5.x) send this value in the API
request; others derive it from state but don't send it to the provider.

Whether [`Self::phase`] was reported by the provider or inferred from
tool-call presence. A derived phase carries no information beyond
"this message called tools", so consumers that need a real
classification must be able to tell the two apart.

SavedReport.description:
A user-saved report definition — a named, persistable wrapper around a
`ReportQuery` with optional dashboard placement metadata.

created_at.description: Timestamp when this resource was created (RFC 3339).

oneOf.description:
Optional dashboard placement metadata. `None` means the report is
"library-only" and not pinned to a dashboard layout.

description.description: Human-readable description. Safe to render in user-facing messages.

name.description: Human-readable name. Safe to render in user-facing messages.

query.description:
The query this report executes when run or exported. Same shape as the
`body` of `POST /v1/reports/query` — see `ReportQuery` for the field
breakdown.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when this resource was last updated (RFC 3339).

SavedReportDashboardMetadata.description:
Dashboard placement metadata attached to a `SavedReport`. Captures how
and where to render the report in the operator dashboard UI.

chart_type.description:
Rendering hint for the UI (e.g. `"line"`, `"bar"`, `"table"`,
`"big_number"`). Free-form string — the server doesn't enforce a
closed set so new chart types can roll out client-side first.

position.description:
Sort key within `section`. Lower values render first. `None` means
"place at the end".

section.description:
Dashboard section/group this report belongs to (free-form bucket name
like `"Operations"` or `"Finance"`). Used to cluster related reports
in the UI.

title.description: Human-readable title. Safe to render in user-facing messages.

completed_at.description: Timestamp when this resource completed, if any (RFC 3339).

created_at.description: Timestamp when this resource was created (RFC 3339).

duration_ms.description: Total execution duration in milliseconds (`completed_at - started_at`). `None` while still running.

error.description: Human-readable error message, populated when this resource is in a failed state.

scheduled_at.description: Timestamp when this resource is scheduled to run (RFC 3339).

started_at.description: Timestamp when this resource started, if any (RFC 3339).

data.description: Page of items returned by this query.

total.description: Total number of items matching the query, across all pages.

catch_up_missed.description: When `true`, missed fires (while the scheduler was down, paused, or unreachable) are queued and run after recovery, subject to `max_catch_up`.

created_at.description: Timestamp when this resource was created (RFC 3339).

cron_expression.description: Cron expression in the standard `min hour day-of-month month day-of-week` form (6 fields with seconds optional). Evaluated in `timezone`.

description.description: Human-readable description. Safe to render in user-facing messages.
description.example: Fires the support-triage agent every night at 02:00 UTC

enabled.description: When `false`, the schedule is paused — kept in storage but never fires until re-enabled.

last_triggered_at.description: Timestamp of the most recent fire (RFC 3339). `None` if never triggered.

max_catch_up.description: Maximum number of missed fires to replay when `catch_up_missed` is `true`. Older missed fires are dropped. `None` means no cap.

max_concurrent.description: Maximum number of overlapping executions allowed. `None` means no limit beyond the worker pool's concurrency.

name.description: Human-readable name. Safe to render in user-facing messages.

next_trigger_at.description: Timestamp of the next scheduled fire (RFC 3339). `None` when the schedule is disabled or the cron expression has no upcoming match.

retry_policy.description:
Optional retry policy for failed runs (provider-specific JSON; see the durable engine's `RetryPolicy`).

target.description: What the schedule invokes when it fires (a session, an agent, an app channel, etc.).

timezone.description: IANA timezone name used to interpret `cron_expression` (e.g. `UTC`, `America/New_York`).

updated_at.description: Timestamp when this resource was last updated (RFC 3339).

avg_duration_ms.description: Average execution duration in milliseconds across `total_executions`. `None` when no executions exist yet.

failed_executions.description: Count of executions that ended in failure (after exhausting retries).

last_execution_status.description:
Status of the most recent execution (one of the `ScheduleExecutionResponse.status` values:

skipped_executions.description: Count of fires that were intentionally skipped (e.g. blocked by `max_concurrent` or disabled mid-fire).

successful_executions.description: Count of executions that completed successfully.

total_executions.description: Total number of executions recorded for this schedule (sum of successful + failed + skipped).

Example: `{"approved": true, "approver": "user_01933b5a00007000800000000000001"}`.

signal_type.description: Signal name. Must match a signal the running workflow listens for.

ServiceKind.description:
A typed service a provider driver can offer.

Drivers declare supported services in code; catalog models persist their
selected service. One provider account composes typed chat, decision and
embedding drivers over shared authentication.

Session.description:
Session - instance of agentic loop execution.
A session represents a single conversation with an agent.

active_schedule_count.description:
Number of active (enabled) schedules for this session.
Populated when the session is fetched for API responses.

activity.description:
Outcome-oriented status derived from `status` and the last turn result.
This is the value the sessions list groups by and the facet rail counts.

agent_id.description: ID of the agent working in this session (format: agent_{32-hex}). Optional.

agent_revision.description:
Revision of the agent's history this session started on, when the
agent had one. `everruns history show <agent> --revision N` shows the
configuration that ran.

archived_at.description:
When this session was archived; `None` means active. Archived sessions
are hidden from default list results and shown by opting in
(`include_archived=true`). Unlike `is_pinned`, archive is a property of
the session itself rather than of the viewer.

blueprint_config.description:
Validated config passed by host at blueprint spawn time.
Example: `{"target_repo": "acme/everruns"}`.

blueprint_id.description:
Blueprint ID. When set, reason_activity and act_activity build RuntimeAgent
from the blueprint definition instead of from harness_id/agent_id.

capabilities.description:
Session-level capabilities (additive to agent capabilities).
Applied after agent capabilities when building RuntimeAgent.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the session was created.

oneOf.description: Effective human owner summary.

event_count.description:
Total events recorded for this session (EVE-868). Derived from the
session's event sequence rather than counted, so the session detail
tab bar costs no extra scan over `events`.
`None` on payloads built outside the database read path.

features.description:
Aggregated UI features from all active capabilities (harness + agent + session).
Computed at read time from the capability registry.
Known features: "file_system", "schedules", "secrets", "key_value",
"sql_database", "leased_resources".

file_count.description:
Non-directory files in this session's workspace (EVE-868). Read from
`workspaces.file_count`. Counts persisted files only: capability-provided
virtual mounts are served from memory and are not included.

finished_at.description: Timestamp when the session finished (completed or failed).

forked_from_sequence.description:
Parent event sequence the fork was taken at (the fork point). NULL unless
this session is a fork.

forked_from_session_id.description:
Session this one was forked from. NULL for sessions that were not forked.
Distinct from `parent_session_id` (subagent nesting): forking is a
user-initiated "branch from here" relationship.

goal.description: Session objective visible to the runtime agent at system-prompt level.

harness_id.description: ID of the harness for this session (format: harness_{32-hex}).

hints.description:
Session-level client hints — arbitrary key-value pairs declared by the
client at session creation time. These are defaults for every turn;
per-message `controls.hints` override these key-by-key (shallow merge).

Examples: `{"setup_connection": true, "rich_media": true}`

id.description: Unique identifier for the session (format: session_{32-hex}).

initial_files.description:
Starting files for a new file tree (additive to agent/harness files).
Matching paths override earlier layers. Rejected when attaching workspace_id.

is_pinned.description:
Whether this session is pinned by the current user.
Only populated when the request has an authenticated user context.

locale.description: Locale for localized agent behavior and formatting (BCP 47, e.g. `uk-UA`).

max_iterations.description: Maximum number of LLM iterations per turn for this session.

mcpServers.description: Remote MCP servers scoped to this session only.

model_id.description:
LLM model ID to use for this session (format: model_{32-hex}).
Overrides the agent's default model if set.

oneOf.description:
Network access list controlling which hosts/URLs this session can reach.
Merged with harness and agent layers (allowed: intersect, blocked: union).

organization_id.description: Organization this session belongs to (format: org_{32-hex}).

output_preview.description: Preview text from the last assistant response (truncated).
output_preview.example: Here is a Q3 plan covering the three pillars we discussed...

oneOf.description: Owning principal summary.

parallel_tool_calls.description:
Request-level parallel tool calling preference (EVE-598).

`None` (default) preserves provider defaults. `Some(true)` signals the
provider that parallel tool calls are wanted; `Some(false)` requests at
most one tool call per turn and forces serial execution. Merged across
harness/agent/session layers (overlay wins).

parent_session_id.description:
Parent session that spawned this subagent. NULL for top-level sessions.
Used to compute governed subagent delegation depth.

playground_user_id.description: Fixed end-user identity for a Playground conversation; independent of the resident service.

preview.description: Preview text from the first user message (truncated).
preview.example: Help me draft the Q3 marketing plan

resolved_owner_user_id.description: Denormalized effective human owner of the owning principal lineage.

run_summary.description:
Generated one-sentence description of what the run did, and where it
failed (EVE-867). Absent until a terminal turn has been summarised, and
always absent for chat threads and for deployments with no utility LLM,
so a reader must have a fallback rather than treating this as required.
run_summary.example: Ran the nightly report and failed posting it to Slack: channel_not_found.

source.description: How this session was started. Server-owned for every ingress path.

started_at.description: Timestamp when the session started executing.

status.description: Current execution status of the session.

system_prompt.description:
Session-level system prompt override.
Prepended to the agent's system prompt when building RuntimeAgent.

tags.description: Tags for organizing and filtering sessions.

task_count.description:
Background work owned by this session — subagents, external agents and
background tools (EVE-868). Read from `sessions.task_count`. This is
what the Work tab holds; `active_schedule_count` describes only the
schedules it also lists.

title.description: Human-readable title for the session.

tools.description: Client-side tools for this session (additive to agent tools).

updated_at.description: Timestamp when the session was last updated.

oneOf.description: Cumulative token usage for all LLM calls in this session.

virtual_user_id.description: Optional resident virtual user for unattended/background execution.

workspace_id.description:
Workspace this session is attached to (format: wsp_{32-hex}). Owns the
session's virtual filesystem. For the default 1:1 case this mirrors the
session id, but clients should read it here rather than deriving it.

SessionActivatedData.description: Data for session.activated event (turn started, session now active)

input_message_id.description: Input message ID that triggered the turn

turn_id.description: Turn ID that activated the session

SessionActivity.description:
Outcome-oriented view of a session, as the sessions list and facet rail
present it. Derived from the session's execution status plus the outcome of
its most recent turn — `SessionStatus` alone has no notion of failure.

SessionBinding.description:
What identity keys a session, for every exposure and every transport.

One enum replaces the former `SessionStrategy` (messaging channels) and
`InvocationSessionMode` (triggers and request/reply endpoints), which asked
the same question with disjoint vocabularies and forced every new surface to
pick a side (EVE-1005).

**The serialized values are deliberately the legacy ones.** Every variant
renames in Rust but serializes exactly as it did before, with the new name
accepted as a read alias. Persisted `channel_config` JSONB therefore needs no
migration, and the API and UI keep exchanging the values they already do.
Moving the wire vocabulary is a separate, migration-bearing change.

`Requester` keys on the **transport's own external actor id** — the Slack
user id, the Public Chat visitor id — never on an Everruns principal. Those
actors are unrelated to Everruns accounts (a Public Chat visitor is anonymous
or Google-signed-in), so there is one consistent answer rather than a split
variant: whatever the transport calls the requester, scoped by the
`{platform}:` tag prefix that already namespaces it.

SessionContextReport.description:
Token-budget report for a session — a model-aware breakdown of the
context window into named sections plus per-source contributions, so
callers can answer "what's filling the context?" without reverse-
engineering the prompt assembly.

contributions.description: Per-source token contributions (per-tool, per-capability, per-message) for attribution.

oneOf.description: Cumulative LLM usage observed across the session so far (token + cost rollup).

estimated_input_tokens.description: Estimated number of input tokens consumed by the next generation given the current context.

model.description: Model identifier the report's token estimates target (used to scope context-window math).

sections.description: Logical sections of the assembled context (system prompt, tool defs, message history, etc.) for inspection.

session_id.description: Prefixed session identifier this report describes.

SessionFacetCount.description: One bucket of a sessions facet dimension.

value.description: The dimension value: an activity, a source, or an agent's public id.

SessionFacetsResponse.description:
Facet-rail counts and masthead metrics for the sessions surface (EVE-852).

Every count is aggregated server-side over the same filter predicate as
`GET /v1/sessions`, so a client never derives them by paging the list. Each
facet dimension is counted with the other filters applied but its own
selection excluded, which is what lets the rail offer multi-select.

active_now.description: Sessions executing a turn or awaiting client tool results right now.

by_agent.description:
Counts per agent, keyed by the agent's public id. Sessions with no
agent are omitted.

failed_today.description: Sessions whose most recent turn failed or was cancelled today (UTC).

p95_duration_ms.description: 95th percentile session duration over the filtered set, milliseconds.

tokens_today.description: Tokens consumed by sessions created today (UTC).

Operator action to take against a session's managed sandbox. `Pause`

How a session came into existence.

Closed set: the sessions facet rail enumerates every variant, so the value

clients may only declare the two variants they can legitimately be
(`Chat` and `Api`), which keeps a facet like "started by a schedule"

SideEffectClass.description:
How many times a tool call may safely be executed given the same inputs.

Used by the durable Act activity (EVE-530) to decide what to do when a
prior execution attempt left a `running` claim in `durable_tool_results`:

* `Pure` / `Idempotent` — the running claim is stale; re-execute freely.
* `AtMostOnce` — never re-execute from a stale running claim; settle it
  as `interrupted` and surface an uncertain result to the model instead.

When unset (`None`), the conservative default is `AtMostOnce`.

Speed level for models that expose a latency/price service tier.
Wire values map 1:1 to the OpenAI `service_tier` request parameter:

premium), `fast` (OpenAI's current name for `priority`; the API accepts

TextAnnotation.description:
A claim-level citation attached to a span of generated text.

The single shared type across every citation capability: a text span linked
to a source. Producers agree only on this render contract — each capability
keeps its own richer representation (e.g. `KnowledgeIndexCitation`) and maps

Opaque producer id (e.g. `kchk_…`, `kbe_…`, a URL hash). Not interpreted
by the render contract.

Capability id that produced this annotation (e.g. `citation_retrieval`).
Lets the UI and evals attribute and filter each citation by feed.

Verification verdict, filled by the `citation_verification` capability.
Absent means unverified (not "unsupported").

annotations.description:
Claim-level citations attached to spans of `text`.

The narrow render contract shared by all citation capabilities. Empty for non-cited text, so the wire shape of
existing messages is unchanged.

TokenUsage.description:
Token usage statistics

Tracks token consumption per LLM call including cache tokens for cost
optimization.

# Disjoint bucket convention

Prompt token buckets are **disjoint** (non-overlapping). Drivers normalize
provider wire formats at the boundary so this holds for every provider:

```text
total_prompt = input_tokens + cache_read_tokens + cache_creation_tokens
```

- `input_tokens` — non-cached prompt tokens only.
- `cache_read_tokens` — tokens served from cache, never counted in
  `input_tokens`.
- `cache_creation_tokens` — tokens written to cache, never counted in
  `input_tokens`.

Inclusive providers (OpenAI Responses / Chat Completions, Gemini) report a
prompt count that *includes* cached reads; their drivers subtract the cached
subset so the value stored here is the non-cached remainder. Anthropic /
Bedrock already report disjoint buckets. Cost is therefore uniform across
providers (`input·in + cache_read·cr + cache_creation·cw + output·out`);
consumers must not re-derive a non-cached input by subtracting cache reads.

actual_cost_usd.description:
Actual cost of this generation in USD, as reported by the provider inline
(e.g. OpenRouter's `usage.cost`, which reflects real post-routing/BYOK/cache
pricing). `None` for providers that do not return a cost.

cache_creation_tokens.description: Number of tokens written to cache, disjoint from `input_tokens`

cache_read_tokens.description: Number of tokens read from cache (reduces cost), disjoint from `input_tokens`

effective_cost_usd.description:
Best-effort USD cost when it cannot be derived from actual/estimated
alone: already-aggregated usage, or a generation carrying a cost that
belongs to neither slot. Per-generation usage normally leaves this unset
and derives the effective cost from actual-else-estimated; the exception
is a turn whose compaction cost is folded in, where the combined total
has to live here precisely so the generation's own actual-vs-estimated
distinction survives (EVE-895).

estimated_cost_usd.description:
Estimated cost of this generation in USD, derived from the model's static
price-table profile. Computed whenever a profile with cost data exists,
independently of `actual_cost_usd`, so estimate-vs-actual drift can be
reconciled. `None` when there is no profile cost data for the model.

input_tokens.description:
Number of non-cached prompt tokens (cached reads/writes are tracked
separately; see the disjoint bucket convention on the struct)

ToolHints.description:
Semantic hints describing a tool's behavioral properties.

Follows the MCP tool annotations convention (readOnlyHint, destructiveHint,
idempotentHint, openWorldHint) plus everruns-specific hints. All fields are
optional booleans — `None` means "unknown/unspecified". Consumers should
treat `None` as the conservative default (e.g., assume not readonly, assume
not idempotent).

These hints are informational — they do not enforce policy. Use `ToolPolicy`
for execution gating (auto vs requires_approval).

capability_id.description:
Capability that contributed this tool definition.

Reporting uses this attribution only as metadata. It must never contain
tool arguments, results, prompts, or any other sensitive payload.

capability_name.description: Human-readable capability name snapshot for reporting.

concurrency_class.description:
Scheduling conflict key. Tool calls within the same act batch that share
a non-empty `concurrency_class` are executed sequentially in arrival
order; calls in different classes (or with no class) run concurrently.

Set this on tools that mutate shared session state so that, e.g., two
file writes or two SQL mutations in one batch do not race. Read-only
tools should leave this `None` so they always parallelize. See
`everruns-engine`'s tool scheduler for how the act phase consumes it.

cpu_bound.description:
Tool performs significant CPU-bound or otherwise non-yielding work in
process (e.g. an in-process interpreter). When true, the act scheduler
runs the call on its own task (`tokio::spawn`) so a long CPU burst does
not starve the cooperative polling of I/O-bound tools in the same batch.

Distinct from `long_running`, which describes wall-clock time for
I/O-bound work (those tools yield at await points and need no offload).

destructive.description:
Tool may irreversibly destroy or delete data.
Subset of non-readonly — a tool can be non-readonly (writes) without
being destructive (e.g., create/update operations).

idempotent.description:
Calling the tool repeatedly with the same arguments produces the same
effect. Safe to retry on transient failures.

long_running.description:
Tool may take significant time to complete (> ~5s typical).
Useful for clients to show progress indicators and set timeouts.

metadata.description:
Host-owned annotations that core does not interpret.

The typed hints above are the vocabulary core itself reasons about. This
is the escape hatch for everything a *host* wants to carry alongside a
tool — risk tiers for an approval UI, presentation hints, an embedder's
routing keys — without adding a field to core for each one. Core reads
nothing here and no driver sends it to a provider; it travels with the
definition so a consumer sees it at the point of decision (e.g. a
`PreToolUseHook` gating on what the tool declared).

The schema belongs to whoever writes it. Never put credentials or other
sensitive payload here: like the rest of the definition, it is persisted
and surfaced to clients.

narration_noun.description:
Entity noun for operation-based narration (e.g. "agent", "harness").
When set, the narration system reads the `operation` argument and
produces verb-based narration like "Created agent: Neon Cartographer"
instead of the generic "Ran Manage Agents".

open_world.description:
Tool interacts with external entities beyond the local system
(network calls, third-party APIs, cloud services).

persist_output.description:
Tool output should be persisted to session VFS before truncation.
When set, the `tool_output_persistence` capability (EVE-222, EVE-245) writes
stdout to `/outputs/{tool_call_id}.stdout` and stderr to
`/outputs/{tool_call_id}.stderr`, injecting `full_output`, `total_lines`,
and `output_files` into the result.

readonly.description:
Tool does not modify any state (read-only queries, lookups).
When true: safe to call speculatively, result can be cached.

requires_secrets.description:
Tool requires API keys, credentials, or other secrets to function.
Useful for UI to show connection prompts and for LLMs to anticipate
authentication failures.

oneOf.description:
Replay-safety class used by the durable Act activity (EVE-530).

Controls what happens when a worker reclaims a stale `running` claim:
`Pure`/`Idempotent` tools are re-executed; `AtMostOnce` tools are
settled as `interrupted` to prevent double side-effects.

`None` is treated conservatively as `AtMostOnce`.

stays_direct.description:
Tool must stay a direct tool call and never runs from inside a shell
script (`tools_in_shell`): it pauses or shapes the turn, or its result
only makes sense to the model directly.

supports_background.description:
Tool supports detached background execution via `spawn_background`.
When true, the tool may be executed asynchronously outside the current
foreground tool call and report status back later.

ToolNestedCallData.description:

A shell script called one of the agent's tools through the `tools` command,
inside the `bash` call named by `parent_tool_call_id`. Informational: the
model did not make this call, so there is no matching `tool.started` /
`tool.completed` or tool-result message; the `bash` result carries what the
script printed.

This enables live output rendering (e.g., bash stdout/stderr, command output)

produces streamed output (bashkit, Daytona exec, subagent speech, etc.).

The consumer accumulates deltas by tool_call_id for display. The final
tool.completed result is authoritative — deltas are informational only.

open and Slack stays silent, never falling back to the deployment.

allOf.description:
Agent configuration for agentic loop.
An agent defines the behavior and capabilities of an AI assistant.

archived_at.description: Timestamp when the agent was archived.

oneOf.description:
Avatar shown wherever the agent appears: the UI, the A2A Agent Card and
its Slack app. Set with `PUT /v1/agents/{agent_id}/avatar`.

capabilities.description:
Capabilities enabled for this agent with per-agent configuration.
Capabilities add tools and system prompt modifications.

communication.description:
How the agent talks to people. `direct` (default): its replies are
what it writes. `explicit`: what it writes is private working notes,
and people see only the messages it sends with `send_message`. Applies
on every surface: web chat, API, Slack, A2A, AG-UI, MCP.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the agent was created.

default_model_id.description:
Default LLM model ID for this agent.
Can be overridden at the session level.

deleted_at.description: Timestamp when the agent was deleted.

description.description: Human-readable description of what the agent does.
description.example: Handles refund and shipping questions; escalates billing disputes.

display_name.description:
Human-readable display name shown in UI (e.g. "Customer Support Agent").
Falls back to `name` when absent.

exposed.description:
Whether any endpoint on this agent is currently live. Derived from the
endpoint rows on read and never stored: a stored flag would be a second
writer for state the endpoints already own.

exposures_suspended.description:
Incident switch: when true, no endpoint on this agent accepts traffic
(EVE-1007). Distinct from archiving — it leaves per-endpoint status
untouched so clearing it restores exactly the previously live set.

forked_from_agent_id.description: Source agent for a forked agent.

harness_id.description: Harness that supplies the base execution environment for this agent.

id.description:
External identifier (agent_<32-hex>). Shown as "id" in API.
Client-supplied or auto-generated.

initial_files.description: Starter files copied into each new session for this agent.

intro_markdown.description:
Optional Markdown intro rendered as an intro box at the top of a fresh
Platform Chat thread. Images are allowed. Wins over the harness intro.
Hidden once the user inputs.
intro_markdown.example: Hey, I'm Ava. Ask me anything about your account.

is_built_in.description:
Built-in agents (Platform Chat) are provisioned by the platform and
are read-only: they cannot be modified or deleted via the API. Copy
one to get an editable version.

max_iterations.description: Maximum number of LLM iterations per turn for this agent.

mcpServers.description: Remote MCP servers scoped to this agent and inherited by its sessions.

name.description: Name, unique per org (e.g. "customer-support").

oneOf.description:
Network access list controlling which hosts/URLs agent sessions can reach.
Merged with harness and session layers (allowed: intersect, blocked: union).

parallel_tool_calls.description:
Request-level parallel tool calling preference (EVE-598).

`None` (default) preserves provider defaults. `Some(true)` signals the
provider that parallel tool calls are wanted; `Some(false)` requests at
most one tool call per turn and forces serial execution. Merged across
harness/agent/session layers (overlay wins).

service_virtual_user_id.description: Org-scoped service account used when a tool acts as the agent.

short_description.description:

chat title once the intro is hidden. Wins over the harness value.

starters.description:
Conversation starters for a fresh Platform Chat thread. Win over the
harness starters when non-empty.

status.description: Current lifecycle status of the agent.

system_prompt.description:
System prompt that defines the agent's behavior.
Sent as the first message in every conversation.

icon.description:

Built-in harnesses declare it in their definition; custom harnesses

initial_files.description: Starter files copied into each new session for this harness.

provider that parallel tool calls are wanted; `Some(false)` requests at
most one tool call per turn and forces serial execution. Merged across

entirely from the parent harness (if any), the agent, the session, and
capability contributions. Empty/whitespace-only values normalize to

allOf.description:
Session - instance of agentic loop execution.
A session represents a single conversation with an agent.

active_schedule_count.description:
Number of active (enabled) schedules for this session.
Populated when the session is fetched for API responses.

activity.description:
Outcome-oriented status derived from `status` and the last turn result.
This is the value the sessions list groups by and the facet rail counts.

agent_id.description: ID of the agent working in this session (format: agent_{32-hex}). Optional.

agent_revision.description:
Revision of the agent's history this session started on, when the
agent had one. `everruns history show <agent> --revision N` shows the
configuration that ran.

archived_at.description:
When this session was archived; `None` means active. Archived sessions
are hidden from default list results and shown by opting in
(`include_archived=true`). Unlike `is_pinned`, archive is a property of
the session itself rather than of the viewer.

blueprint_config.description:
Validated config passed by host at blueprint spawn time.
Example: `{"target_repo": "acme/everruns"}`.

blueprint_id.description:
Blueprint ID. When set, reason_activity and act_activity build RuntimeAgent
from the blueprint definition instead of from harness_id/agent_id.

capabilities.description:
Session-level capabilities (additive to agent capabilities).
Applied after agent capabilities when building RuntimeAgent.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the session was created.

oneOf.description: Effective human owner summary.

event_count.description:
Total events recorded for this session (EVE-868). Derived from the
session's event sequence rather than counted, so the session detail
tab bar costs no extra scan over `events`.
`None` on payloads built outside the database read path.

features.description:
Aggregated UI features from all active capabilities (harness + agent + session).
Computed at read time from the capability registry.
Known features: "file_system", "schedules", "secrets", "key_value",
"sql_database", "leased_resources".

file_count.description:
Non-directory files in this session's workspace (EVE-868). Read from
`workspaces.file_count`. Counts persisted files only: capability-provided
virtual mounts are served from memory and are not included.

finished_at.description: Timestamp when the session finished (completed or failed).

forked_from_sequence.description:
Parent event sequence the fork was taken at (the fork point). NULL unless
this session is a fork.

forked_from_session_id.description:
Session this one was forked from. NULL for sessions that were not forked.
Distinct from `parent_session_id` (subagent nesting): forking is a
user-initiated "branch from here" relationship.

goal.description: Session objective visible to the runtime agent at system-prompt level.

harness_id.description: ID of the harness for this session (format: harness_{32-hex}).

hints.description:
Session-level client hints — arbitrary key-value pairs declared by the
client at session creation time. These are defaults for every turn;
per-message `controls.hints` override these key-by-key (shallow merge).

Examples: `{"setup_connection": true, "rich_media": true}`

id.description: Unique identifier for the session (format: session_{32-hex}).

initial_files.description:
Starting files for a new file tree (additive to agent/harness files).
Matching paths override earlier layers. Rejected when attaching workspace_id.

is_pinned.description:
Whether this session is pinned by the current user.
Only populated when the request has an authenticated user context.

locale.description: Locale for localized agent behavior and formatting (BCP 47, e.g. `uk-UA`).

max_iterations.description: Maximum number of LLM iterations per turn for this session.

mcpServers.description: Remote MCP servers scoped to this session only.

model_id.description:
LLM model ID to use for this session (format: model_{32-hex}).
Overrides the agent's default model if set.

oneOf.description:
Network access list controlling which hosts/URLs this session can reach.
Merged with harness and agent layers (allowed: intersect, blocked: union).

organization_id.description: Organization this session belongs to (format: org_{32-hex}).

output_preview.description: Preview text from the last assistant response (truncated).
output_preview.example: Here is a Q3 plan covering the three pillars we discussed...

oneOf.description: Owning principal summary.

parallel_tool_calls.description:
Request-level parallel tool calling preference (EVE-598).

`None` (default) preserves provider defaults. `Some(true)` signals the
provider that parallel tool calls are wanted; `Some(false)` requests at
most one tool call per turn and forces serial execution. Merged across
harness/agent/session layers (overlay wins).

parent_session_id.description:
Parent session that spawned this subagent. NULL for top-level sessions.
Used to compute governed subagent delegation depth.

playground_user_id.description: Fixed end-user identity for a Playground conversation; independent of the resident service.

preview.description: Preview text from the first user message (truncated).
preview.example: Help me draft the Q3 marketing plan

resolved_owner_user_id.description: Denormalized effective human owner of the owning principal lineage.

run_summary.description:
Generated one-sentence description of what the run did, and where it
failed (EVE-867). Absent until a terminal turn has been summarised, and
always absent for chat threads and for deployments with no utility LLM,
so a reader must have a fallback rather than treating this as required.
run_summary.example: Ran the nightly report and failed posting it to Slack: channel_not_found.

source.description: How this session was started. Server-owned for every ingress path.

started_at.description: Timestamp when the session started executing.

status.description: Current execution status of the session.

system_prompt.description:
Session-level system prompt override.
Prepended to the agent's system prompt when building RuntimeAgent.

tags.description: Tags for organizing and filtering sessions.

task_count.description:
Background work owned by this session — subagents, external agents and
background tools (EVE-868). Read from `sessions.task_count`. This is
what the Work tab holds; `active_schedule_count` describes only the
schedules it also lists.

title.description: Human-readable title for the session.

tools.description: Client-side tools for this session (additive to agent tools).

updated_at.description: Timestamp when the session was last updated.

oneOf.description: Cumulative token usage for all LLM calls in this session.

virtual_user_id.description: Optional resident virtual user for unattended/background execution.

workspace_id.description:
Workspace this session is attached to (format: wsp_{32-hex}). Owns the
session's virtual filesystem. For the default 1:1 case this mirrors the
session id, but clients should read it here rather than deriving it.

draining.description: Workers in `draining` state, finishing in-flight tasks but not accepting new ones.
